opening: PD-1 (Programmed cell death protein 1) located on T cells, binds to PD-L1 (Programmed cell death ligand 1) on cancer cells, to suppress T cell activation and enable immune evasion.Hitherto, reviews have mainly highlighted the role of PD-1/ PD-L1 in anti-cancer immunomodulation, anti-cancer therapy resistance, and immune-related adverse events.However, there are critical modes of enhancement of therapeutic efficacy, which remain underappreciated.This review provides a holistic perspective on: (a) a comprehensive analysis of recent clinical trials targeting PD-1/PD-L1, specifically on the use of immune checkpoint i a comprehensive analysis of recent clinical trials targeting PD-1/PD-L1, specifically on the use of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs); (b) the underlying molecular mechanisms of immune surveillance; (c) the role of ubiquitin-mediated post-translational modifications (PTMs, viz the ubiquitin machinery); and (d) the gut microbiome crosstalk with the PD-1/PD-L1 axis, which influences the tumor microenvironment (TME).Clarity gained from opinions exerted from these four factors, in this review, will provide insights on improving cancer prevention, diagnosis, and treatment, thus bridging translational research to th ll provide insights on improving cancer prevention, diagnosis, and treatment, thus bridging translational research to the clinic.These standpoints will be pres
